newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS UPDATE - JAN 27.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS UPDATE - JAN 27.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:

--The national economy minister and the Bank of Greece have agreed on ambitious changes to the banking system which will boost competitiveness and restructure the system, in light of the final phase of Economic and Monetary Union.
--Export firms on the Athens Stock Exchange and those with loans in mark are the big winners in the recent rise of the dollar, which looks set to continue.

--Plans to harmonise Greek legislation governing mutual funds with Community laws are taking shape with the legal services of the Union of Institutional Investors presenting legislation to the Capital Market Commission in the context of amendments to the law on mutual funds.

--The government is expected to give increases of above forecast inflation - but lower than 1996 levels - to employees at public organisations and utilities (DEKO) this year. The biggest increases will be given to workers at the Exports Promotion Organisation (18.9 percent), which falls under the supervision of the national economy ministry.

--Ergobank is adopting an agressive investment policy, according to a recent bank publication. The bank's share capital increase (already approved by the stock exchange) will finance investment programmes and the possible establishment of a new subsidiary company.
--Problems faced by foreign tourists in Greece, the low quality of services and lack of infrastructure are the reasons behind the fall in visitors to Greece over the past two years.

--Hopes of a dramatic increase in profits in 1996 for technical companies listed on the Athens bourse failed to be realised. Construction companies are optimistic however about 1997, since 300 billion drachmas worth of projects will be auctioned in the first half-year alone.
--The sudden rise in the dollar will mean more expensive imports from the US. Our times, an academic says, could be called the "casino-capitalism" epoch, leading us to "crazed speculation".

--National Economy and Finance Minister Yannos Papandoniou is under strong pressure to satisfy union demands at DEKOs for wage increases of above the 7.0 percent foreseen in the government's incomes policy.

--1997 will be a cornerstone year for banks with at least three demanding new capital from the market in the next six months with at most two state-run banks changing hands. Others will take their chances on the bourse, while the government promotes less but stronger banking groups.

--The national economy and finance ministry has prepared a wider floatation policy for state-run companies, as part of efforts to boost competition and trim back the role of the state. Two possibilities for OTE (Greece's telecoms organisation) are being considered: another share float, which would boost revenues for the state, or a share capital increase, which would boost revenue for the company.

--The appointment of a management consultant at the Ionian Bank as well as a volley of reports about the Macedonia-Thrace BAnk is an indication of speedy developments in the sector. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
